sources.citation: Muniru, John (transcriber). 2015. Wordlist: Shau [sqh], Shau village. Nigerian Word List (Hausa version) elicitation form, dated 5 Feb 2015, Toro LGA, Bauchi State; 15 pp. + cover, handwritten. SIL Language & Culture Archives entry 83804 (Language Assessment data set; draft posted 'as is'). Description: 'The Shau language is Dormant and there were very few informants who could remember any words in the language.. the word collection was a collaborative effort.' Extent: '15 pages+5 lexical entries'.
sources.note: No phonology content: scanned handwritten wordlist form (no text; page scan inspected). Almost every item is marked 'd/k' (don't know); a handful of remembered forms are written with acute/grave tone marks (e.g. items 8-10 on p.1). Tone marks in a wordlist without any statement = wordlist-only data, not a prosodic statement. Confirms the language was dormant in 2015 (rememberers only).

sources.note: Second-hand (Blench 2020, AuÜ 93: 57, held): 'Shimizu (1979, 1982a) usually transcribes the tonal systems in his lists as High and Low or High, Low and Downstep and he reconstructs the latter for his Proto-North-Jos' -- i.e. this work reconstructs a Proto-Northern-Jos prosodic system with High, Low and downstep (and a consonant system, p.172, and noun-class system, p.178) from daughter languages that include Shau; it is the only place a tonal analysis drawing on Shau forms is likely to exist beyond the tone-marked 1982a wordlist.
